source_name: ČBA – Průzkumy a indexy ("Češi a platební styk" survey series)
why_relevant: Recurring ČBA consumer survey on payment behaviour — share of card vs cash use, debit vs credit card penetration, contactless/mobile adoption. Editions found for 2019, 2020, 2021; the series is the association's own demand-side counterpart to SBK's supply-side card volumes and is directly on-topic for cash usage.

source_name: ČBA – Statistika (glossary/statistics landing)
why_relevant: Appears in search as ČBA's 'Statistika' entry point but on fetch resolved mainly to a definitional/glossary page rather than a data index. Worth tracking as a possible route into ČBA statistical outputs, but ČBA Monitor is the substantive data home.

source_name: Czech Banking Association – English site (czech-ba.cz)
why_relevant: English-language mirror/parallel presence of ČBA, useful for English terminology, EBF-facing positions and for cross-checking membership counts (~33 banks, ~99% of sector). Also the natural landing page for international-audience publications.

source_name: European Banking Federation (EBF) – national member associations
why_relevant: Supranational pointer confirming ČBA as the recognised CZ national banking association (full EBF member since 1 July 2004) and providing a cross-country frame for comparing CZ association-published data with the ~32 other national associations.

source_name: Česká leasingová a finanční asociace (ČLFA) – Statistiky
why_relevant: Quarterly and annual statistics on leasing, non-bank credit and factoring in CZ, with an explicit English-titled quarterly series. Members reportedly cover ~86% of business financing, ~83% of consumer financing and ~95% of factoring, so the aggregates approximate the whole non-bank finance market — the segment ČNB statistics cover least well.

source_name: ČLFA – Členské společnosti (member directory)
why_relevant: Directory of ~34 specialised finance companies (leasing, consumer credit, instalment sales, factoring) with a per-company detail page. Enumerates the non-bank lender actor set that does not appear on ČBA's list.

source_name: ČLFA – Asociace factoringových společností ČR statistics
why_relevant: Factoring-market statistics of the Asociace factoringových společností ČR, hosted within ČLFA. Members reportedly represent ~95% of the CZ factoring market — a receivables-finance segment adjacent to payments and merchant working capital.

source_name: AKAT ČR – Zveřejněná data (published capital-market data)
why_relevant: Asociace pro kapitálový trh ČR publishes quarterly aggregated data on assets under management and fund distribution by member, including league tables of the largest distributors (Česká spořitelna, ČSOB, KB, Conseq, Amundi). Recent releases report total investments in CZ crossing CZK 4 trillion. Gives per-institution market shares in savings/investment that banks do not publish comparably.

source_name: AKAT ČR – Členové asociace
why_relevant: Over 100 members: domestic investment companies, foreign fund managers distributing in CZ, custodians and other capital-market service providers. Enumerates an actor set only partially overlapping banks and fintechs.

source_name: AKAT – legacy site archive (akatcr-puvodni.cz)
why_relevant: Old AKAT website still serving historical press releases and statistics PDFs (e.g. custodian securities-value releases). Useful for back-filling time series that the redesigned site may no longer expose.

source_name: Česká fintech asociace (ČEFTAS / Czech Fintech Association) – Členové
why_relevant: Directory of 80+ members spanning fintechs, banks, PSPs, legal firms and software houses (observed logos include AEVI, Deloitte, Home Credit; press reports add Adyen and Centrální depozitář cenných papírů). This is the best single enumeration of the CZ fintech/payments innovation actor set, including terminal/POS-adjacent vendors relevant to a payments-hardware view.

source_name: Asociace poskytovatelů nebankovních úvěrů (APNÚ)
why_relevant: Association of ~14 ČNB-licensed non-bank consumer-credit providers. Publishes aggregated lending volumes (reported ~CZK 6.9bn vs 5.8bn the prior year) and loan-purpose breakdowns, and in 2025 launched its own APNÚ credit register — a register is itself a durable data asset and a pointer to the member set.

source_name: Asociace poskytovatelů platebních služeb ČR (ASPPS)
why_relevant: A CZ association specifically of payment service providers (IČO 04387783), positioned around compliance with the Payment Systems Act for online and offline PSPs. Directly on-cell for payments: potentially enumerates non-bank PSPs/payment institutions that neither ČBA nor SBK covers. Small and low-profile — treat scale and activity level as unverified.

source_name: Asociace českých stavebních spořitelen (AČSS) – Vývoj statistik
why_relevant: Building-savings sector statistics and downloadable charts for the five member stavební spořitelny, with a dedicated journalists/experts section. Self-declared source of the underlying data is the Ministry of Finance, so this is a curated re-publication — convenient long time series, but cite the ministry as the primary.

source_name: AČSS – Členové AČSS (member register)
why_relevant: Complete enumeration of the CZ building-savings sub-sector (Českomoravská stavební spořitelna, Stavební spořitelna České spořitelny, Modrá pyramida, Raiffeisen stavební spořitelna, ČSOB Stavební spořitelna / Wüstenrot legacy) — a closed set of 5 institutions, each with its own detail page.

source_name: Association registry entries in Czech commercial/NGO registers (ARES / Obchodní rejstřík mirrors)
why_relevant: Every CZ trade body is a registered z.s./zájmové sdružení with an IČO (ČBA 45772193, Česká fintech asociace 05320534, APNÚ 02734311, ASPPS 04387783, SBK 64933849, AKAT 65399501). Registry mirrors give founding dates, statutory bodies, registered address and filed documents (including statutes and, sometimes, annual reports) — a way to confirm an association is live and to date structural changes independently of its own website.

source_name: LobbyFacts / EU Transparency Register datacard – Česká bankovní asociace
why_relevant: Reveals ČBA indirectly: EU Transparency Register filings disclose declared budget, staff, EU-level policy interests and meeting records. Useful for gauging the association's capacity and priorities, and for detecting which payment-policy files it is actively working — information the association's own site does not present.

source_name: Trade-press amplification of association statistics (ČeskéNoviny, Hypoindex, Měšec, Peníze.cz, Lupa, iProsperita)
why_relevant: Czech financial trade press reliably republishes association releases (ČLFA quarterly volumes, ČBA Hypomonitor, AKAT quarterly investments, APEK payment-method findings) often with figures quoted in the headline. Valuable as an early-warning trigger that a new association dataset exists, and as a fallback when the association's own archive is thin — but always resolve back to the association's primary release.

source_name: Mastercard Newsroom – Czech edition (Tiskové centrum, cs-cz)
why_relevant: Scheme-issued, CZ-specific press releases carrying contactless share, tokenisation share, mobile-payment penetration, merchant-acceptance milestones and Mastercard's European Payment League country rankings — figures that do not appear in CNB aggregates.

source_name: Mastercard Newsroom – Europe (English)
why_relevant: European-level scheme releases regularly break out Czech Republic in cross-country comparisons (SpendingPulse growth forecasts, holiday ticket sizes, experience-economy spend), giving CZ figures benchmarked against peers.

source_name: Visa Česká republika – Newsroom / tiskové zprávy
why_relevant: Visa's CZ country site publishes localised releases with CZ-only survey and transaction data (share of Czechs preferring digital payment, e-commerce abandonment by payment method, Česko platí kartou terminal programme, Visa Awards CZ).

source_name: Visa Česká republika press archive on Mynewsdesk
source_subtype: PR wire mirror of scheme releases
why_relevant: Third-party PR-distribution mirror of Visa CZ releases — plain HTML, chronological, usually easier to crawl than visa.cz itself and gives a datestamped archive back in time.

source_name: ČeskéNoviny.cz – Tiskové zprávy (ČTK Protext) channel carrying Visa/Mastercard CZ releases
why_relevant: Scheme CZ press releases are pushed verbatim through the ČTK paid-press channel; full text is public and stable-URL, making it a robust fallback when scheme sites are JS-heavy or reorganised.

source_name: Visa Europe – Fees and Interchange hub (country MIF disclosures)
why_relevant: Regulation (EU) 2015/751 forces Visa to publish domestic multilateral interchange fee schedules per country; this hub is the index from which the dated Czech Republic PDFs hang. Pointer to the authoritative CZ fee series over time.

source_name: Visa – Czech Republic Domestic Multilateral Interchange Fees (PDF series)
why_relevant: The actual CZ consumer/commercial interchange rate card — debit/credit/commercial splits, contactless and card-not-present differentials. Core economics input for acquiring and terminal-market analysis; not published by CNB.

source_name: Mastercard – Czech Republic Domestic Interchange Fees (11Czech.pdf)
why_relevant: Mastercard's CZ intra-country interchange schedule for Mastercard/Maestro POS and ATM transactions — the counterpart to the Visa CZ rate card and the second half of any CZ card-economics picture.

source_name: Mastercard Europe – Merchant Interchange Rates index
why_relevant: Index page linking every European country interchange PDF including Czechia; the durable entry point when file paths change, and it flags effective dates of rate revisions.

source_name: Worldline – Indicative Card Scheme Fee Rates, Czech Republic
why_relevant: Scheme fees (as opposed to interchange) are not published by Visa/Mastercard themselves; a large acquirer's CZ-specific indicative scheme-fee schedule is the practical proxy disclosure, itemising per-transaction and ad-valorem scheme charges applicable in Czechia.
